This ZIP defines a backup string for one member of a FROST group that spends shielded ZEC with Orchard-protocol keys (in the Orchard or Ironwood pool). The string holds the member’s identifier, the threshold, the group size, the member’s signing share and the group’s

. Together with the group’s unified full viewing key, it is enough to rebuild the member in any wallet that implements this ZIP, without the other members being online. Restoring checks the string against the viewing key, which both detects a string from another group and tells the wallet which key derivation the group uses.

Several wallets now offer FROST groups for shielded ZEC: Zkool, Zafe, Konclave, and the Zcash Foundation’s tools. Each one backs up its members in its own format, so a member can only restore their seat in the app that created it. In July 2026, Zkool’s author described the situation: “There is no standard for it. I choose a way that makes it restorable on Zkool only. One day, someone will write a ZIP.”
Since then, Zkool has moved to a minimal backup string (
, Zkool 6.35.0) that holds only what a member needs. This ZIP takes that string as its first version, so that:
a user can move a seat from one wallet to another, or restore it in a different app after losing a device;
a group can mix implementations, which avoids having every signer come from one vendor;
funds stay reachable if one app is abandoned.

Encoders MUST produce lowercase strings. Decoders MUST accept a string that is entirely lowercase or entirely uppercase, and MUST reject a string in mixed case, as Bech32m requires. A wallet can still show the string in uppercase, for instance in a QR code (see [Rationale]), by converting it after encoding.

The human-readable part is the same on Mainnet and Testnet, and the payload names no network: the network is given by the unified full viewing key used to restore. A string paired with another group’s viewing key, on either network, fails the check in [Restore].

Before it shows an address to receive funds, a wallet SHOULD check the viewing key against a source the member trusts, such as the export made with its own string (see [Export]), an address of the group that the member recorded before and that the viewing key gives, or the same viewing key obtained from at least two other members. (whose strings restore under either key, with a different derivation), and a 3-of-5 ZIP 2005 group; an uppercase string; seventeen strings that decoders must reject, two of them for the padding rule and one with a threshold of 1; and four cases that decode but that the restore must reject: a valid string paired with another group’s viewing key, a string whose signing share is not canonical, one whose signing share is zero, and a viewing key with no Orchard component.
